segments.text: So why did I write a second edition of Clean Code?
I wrote the first edition almost two decades ago, and since then, well, I've learned a
thing or two.
So when I thought about writing a second edition, I thought, you know, instead of just punching
up the original manuscript a little bit, I should just rewrite it.
I thought it would be a good idea to include a lot of new languages.
The first edition was all Java, but the second edition has got C and C++ and Python and Go
and JavaScript and Clojure, as well as some Java.
A few of the chapters of the original I left in, but I heavily modified them.
I also added a number of other topics like architecture and design principles.
I talk quite a bit about the solid principles.
I also talk about testing disciplines in the second edition,
and although I focus pretty heavily on test-driven development,
I also mention two other testing disciplines that are not test-first.
Another thing I talk about is the size of functions.
I want to get rid of the controversy over that issue.
Functions should be small, but they don't all have to be four lines long.
John Osterhout, the author of A Philosophy of Software Design, plays a big part in this particular edition.
He and I do not agree on everything, but we have a nice debate which is included in the appendix.
Some of the original authors from the Clean Code book also contributed their new ideas.
So, I think you'll find it a different experience, a broadening experience,
and I hope you enjoy it.
